milestone: Operator directive, live evidence from the deployed SmartWallet Architect: 'Architect failure is provider infrastructure, not an Architect regression' + 'Advisor output is being discarded' + 'Do not call a provider failure DELIVERED.' Explicit scope fence: do not change admission, eligibility, delegation, Gate 1 or Gate 2.
problem: Two independent defects shared one root: `dispatchInformationalProvider()` (`services/financialServices/serviceRequestOrchestrator.ts`, Repair D) already distinguished DELIVERED (a real completed provider result) from UNRESOLVED (the gate allowed but the provider call did not complete) — but it went no further. (1) Every technical provider failure, whether an inference-provider-infrastructure outage or a genuine content/grounding failure, collapsed into the SAME generic 'provider invocation did not complete' reason string, with no way for a caller (the orchestration panel, the Architect route) to distinguish 'every inference provider is down' from 'the Architect itself failed to design something' — live evidence showed Anthropic/OpenAI/Venice all failing (credits/quota/timeout) and the operator-facing surface had no way to say so distinctly. (2) On the SUCCESS path, Advisor's real prose response was hashed into a 16-character `providerResultRef` and the actual text was thrown away before it ever reached the outcome; Architect's success path kept only the artifact id, discarding the title/body a human would need to read without a separate fetch.
observedFailure: Live SmartWallet evidence: Anthropic -> insufficient credits, OpenAI -> insufficient quota, Venice -> timeout, ModelRouter -> 'all providers failed'. The Architect panel and Financial Service orchestration outcome had no distinct representation for this — it read as an generic Architect/service failure, not as 'no inference provider was reachable.'

`runMoneyPennyChat()` returns a real prose answer for Advisor requests, but the orchestrator's dispatch function discarded the text immediately after computing its hash, so no operator-facing surface could ever show what MoneyPenny actually said.
rootCauses: `callStage()` (`services/constitutional/modelRouter.ts`) already throws exactly one distinguishable infrastructure-failure shape — 'all providers failed' — when every provider in the routed target + fallback ladder is unreachable, but nothing downstream of it classified that shape; every catch site treated it as an undifferentiated `Error`.

`dispatchInformationalProvider()`'s success paths were designed around 'preserve an immutable evidence/commitment reference' (Repair D's own stated discipline) without a parallel 'and preserve what a human should actually see' concern — the two were conflated into a single `resultRef` field, so satisfying the evidence-reference requirement necessarily discarded the display value.

The Advisor branch's `.catch(() => null)` actively discarded the real thrown error (whatever its cause) before any classification could occur — a specific instance of the general defect, not a separate one.
resolution: `services/constitutional/modelRouter.ts`: added `INFERENCE_PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE`, `isProviderUnavailableError()` (matches ONLY the exact 'all providers failed' marker `callStage()` throws — never a broader heuristic), `describeInferenceUnavailability()` (bounded to 400 chars; the underlying per-provider messages are already secret-safe response-body slices or timeout strings, confirmed by reading every throw site in `services/experiments/llm.ts`), and `describeProviderLadderAvailability()` (booleans only, never a credential value).

`moneyPennyArchitect.ts::draftFinancialStructure()`: the `callSovereign` catch now classifies via `isProviderUnavailableError` and sets `errorCode: 'INFERENCE_PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE'` on that one shape, leaving every other failure path (grounding failure, empty response) unclassified as before.

`app/api/moneypenny/architect/route.ts`: an `INFERENCE_PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` result now returns HTTP 503 (infrastructure/upstream), not 400 (client error) — the status code itself now tells a caller which kind of failure this is.

`types/financialServices.ts`: added `AdvisorDisplayOutput`/`ArchitectDisplayOutput`/`ProviderDisplayOutput` and `providerOutput`/`errorCode` fields on `FinancialServiceOutcome`, explicitly documented as service-output display data OUTSIDE the frozen VELA-001 Authority/Projection/Authorisation/Execution/ObservedConsequence ontology — additive alongside `providerResultRef`, never a replacement for it.

`services/financialServices/serviceRequestOrchestrator.ts::dispatchInformationalProvider()`: rewritten to return `{ok, resultRef, displayOutput}` on success and `{ok:false, error, errorCode?}` on failure. Advisor's `.catch(() => null)` was replaced with a real try/catch that classifies the thrown error; a successful Advisor call now carries the FULL response text in `displayOutput.text` alongside the unchanged sha256-hash `resultRef` (the evidence reference is never replaced by raw prose — both are preserved, per the operator's explicit instruction). A successful Architect call carries `{title, preview (bounded to 600 chars, with a `truncated` flag), artifactId}` in `displayOutput`, alongside the unchanged `resultRef` = artifact id.

`requestFinancialService()`'s UNRESOLVED/DELIVERED outcome construction now threads `dispatch.errorCode`/`dispatch.displayOutput` into the outcome's new `errorCode`/`providerOutput` fields — the DELIVERED-vs-UNRESOLVED semantics from Repair D are otherwise UNCHANGED.

`ServiceOrchestrationPanel.tsx`: renders `providerOutput` inline (Advisor's full response text; Architect's title + preview + a link to the full artifact when truncated), and renders `errorCode === 'INFERENCE_PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE'` as 'UNRESOLVED — inference provider unavailable' with the bounded diagnostic shown separately from the status badge — never as 'Architect refused.'
rejectedApproaches: Rewriting or forking `draftFinancialStructure()`/`runMoneyPennyChat()` to add provider-failure handling of their own — rejected per the operator's explicit instruction ('Do not rewrite or fork Architect'); the classification lives once in `modelRouter.ts`, at the one throw site every caller already shares.

Replacing `providerResultRef` with the raw prose/artifact body — rejected per the operator's explicit instruction ('Do not replace the evidence reference with raw prose'); `resultRef` (hash or artifact id) and `displayOutput` (the real content) are BOTH preserved, as two distinct fields.

Folding the new display fields into the frozen VELA-001 constitutional-commerce ontology (`types/constitutionalCommerce.ts`) — rejected per the operator's explicit instruction; they live on `types/financialServices.ts`'s `FinancialServiceOutcome`, documented as service output, not a second Authority/Projection/Authorisation mechanism.

A broader heuristic classifier ('this error message looks like an LLM/provider problem') — rejected under the No-Guessing discipline; the classifier matches only the one exact, already-proven throw shape from `callStage()`.
